node.title: Dihedral quotient pencils survive the twenty-fiber SPI interface
node.closure: explicit inversion-quotient pencils give a second unbounded abstract survivor family
node.statement: Let N be a power of two and d in {1,2,4} divide N. For a nonsquare a in mu_(N/d), the pencil u=X^(2d)+a, v=X^d has N/(2d) pairwise-disjoint split squarefree degree-2d fibers, indexed by the fixed-point-free inversion orbits {z,a/z} in mu_(N/d). On N=2097152 the minimum is 262144 fibers. Thus the twenty-fiber exception-SPI interface admits dihedral as well as cyclic quotient survivors; closure must classify or price both using retained heavy-ruling semantics. This is an algebraic route fence, not an MCA counterexample.
